tasks.gr6-limpopo-valley-k2-schroda-t1: Topic: Societies in the Limpopo Valley before Mapungubwe: K2 and Schroda (Grade 6 History, Term 1). Cover that between about AD 900 and AD 1300 the societies of the Limpopo Valley became bigger, more organised and more complex; Schroda (about AD 900 to 1000) where farmers kept cattle, made pottery and had ivory and glass beads that show trade with far away people; K2 (about AD 1000 to 1220), a bigger settlement where cattle were a sign of wealth and leaders became more important; the people moving to Mapungubwe Hill about AD 1220; how archaeologists use objects and remains as evidence; change and continuity (cattle and farming stayed important). Use 'about' for the dates of Schroda and K2; Mapungubwe 1220 to 1300 is exact. Calculate years as end year minus start year. Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-mapungubwe-kingdom-t1: Topic: Mapungubwe, the first state in southern Africa, AD 1220 to 1300 (Grade 6 History, Term 1). Cover that it lasted 80 years; it was ruled by a king who was a sacred leader (believed to have special sacred powers); the king and leaders lived on top of Mapungubwe Hill apart from ordinary people and were buried there; the first stone-walled palace in southern Africa; the first town below the hill where farmers, herders, potters and metalworkers lived; distinct social classes shown by where people lived and by graves (gold on the hill, simple graves below); Mapungubwe as a complex society built by the people of southern Africa, whose earlier home was K2. Tell it as an African achievement. Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-mapungubwe-trade-today-t1: Topic: Mapungubwe: gold, trade and journeys; Mapungubwe today (Grade 6 History, Term 1). Cover the golden rhinoceros and other golden objects (a bowl and a sceptre) found in royal graves on the hill in the 1930s as symbols of royal power and political leadership; trade across Africa and the Indian Ocean (globalisation: places far apart joined by trade); gold and ivory sent away, glass beads and cloth received; traders walking between Mapungubwe and the east coast, the dangers (wild animals, lack of water, getting lost) and how they found their way (landmarks such as hills and rivers, the sun and stars, local guides); today the Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape is a World Heritage Site (named in 2003) and the Order of Mapungubwe is a South African honour (created in 2002). Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-east-coast-trade-great-zimbabwe-t1: Topic: East coast trade and Great Zimbabwe (Grade 6 History, Term 1). Cover change and continuity in trade between the east coast of Africa and settlements inland (inland people sent gold and ivory to the coast; traders from across the Indian Ocean, such as Arabia, Persia and India, brought cloth and glass beads; the trade went on before and after Mapungubwe: continuity), and that when Mapungubwe ended about AD 1300 the centre of trade and power moved north to Great Zimbabwe (change); Great Zimbabwe in present-day Zimbabwe, at its height about AD 1300 to 1450 (about 150 years), built by the ancestors of the Shona people with great stone walls laid without mortar, rulers wealthy from cattle and the gold trade, glass beads and porcelain showing long-distance trade; what Mapungubwe and Great Zimbabwe had in common and how they differed. Use 'about' for the dates of Great Zimbabwe. Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-marco-polo-t1: Topic: Marco Polo, a European explorer in Asia (Grade 6 History, Term 1). Cover that Marco Polo was a merchant's son from Venice who travelled with his father and uncle, left in 1271 and returned in 1295 (24 years), travelled overland along trade routes to China and served the ruler Kublai Khan, that his travels were written in a book (copied by hand because there was no printing press in Europe yet) describing Asian cities, silk, spices, porcelain and paper money, that the book made European traders and explorers more interested in Asia, and that his journey fell in the years of Mapungubwe (AD 1220 to 1300), allowing a comparison of societies in the same period. Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-renaissance-t2: Topic: The Renaissance, Leonardo da Vinci and Galileo (Grade 6 History, Term 2). Cover that Renaissance means rebirth, a time in Europe of new interest in learning, art and science when people observed and tested; the printing press about 1450 helped ideas spread; Leonardo da Vinci (1452 to 1519, 67 years), an Italian painter (Mona Lisa), inventor and scientist; Galileo (1564 to 1642, 78 years), an Italian scientist who used a telescope to see mountains on the Moon and moons around Jupiter and supported the idea that the Earth moves around the sun; Church leaders disagreed with him and limited his freedom; comparing the two. Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-inventions-reasons-exploring-t2: Topic: Why Europeans explored, and the inventions that helped (Grade 6 History, Term 2). Cover the reasons (wealth from spices, silk and gold, a sea route to Asia, spreading Christianity, curiosity and fame), inventions and improvements (magnetic compass, first used in China; astrolabe; better maps; the caravel, a light ship that could sail against the wind; the printing press about 1450), the difference between a reason (why go) and an invention (how it was possible), and that other sailors such as Arab and African sailors already knew these seas. Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-dias-da-gama-t2: Topic: Dias at Mossel Bay and Da Gama's sea route (Grade 6 History, Term 2). Cover that Portugal looked for a sea route to Asia; Bartolomeu Dias sailed round the southern tip of Africa in 1488, landed at what is now Mossel Bay, and turned back because his crew was tired and afraid; the Khoikhoi herders living there with their cattle and the sailors needing fresh water did not understand each other and the meeting turned violent (told from both sides: the sailors needed water, the Khoikhoi protected their water and cattle on their own land); Vasco da Gama set out in 1497 and reached India in 1498 (about one year), nine years after Dias, helped by a local pilot on the east coast of Africa; why the sea route mattered and that it helped some people and harmed others. Use plain, non-graphic words and treat both sides with respect. Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
tasks.gr6-voc-sailors-t2: Topic: The VOC, journeys and a sailor's life (Grade 6 History, Term 2). Cover that the VOC (Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie, the Dutch East India Company) was a Dutch trading company started in 1602 whose ships sailed to Asia for spices and silk, voyages took many months round the southern tip of Africa, life on board was crowded and hard (hard biscuit, salted meat, heavy work, storms, disease), scurvy is caused by too little vitamin C and cured by fresh fruit and vegetables, ships stopped for fresh water and food, and the jobs on board (captain, sailors, soldiers, carpenter, surgeon). Ask simple Grade 6 questions.
